title: An in vivo biosafety-level-2-compatible model of Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection for drug susceptibility testing
protocol: Thaw bacterial stocks based on previously evaluated CFU number.
Pool thawed bacterial stocks together.
Centrifuge pooled bacteria at 10,000 × g for 2 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Remove supernatant from the centrifuged sample.
Resuspend bacteria pellet in PBS-Tween to obtain a suspension of desired CFU in 100 μL.
Prepare at least n + 3 aliquots of 110 μL each, where n is the number of mice to be injected.
Calculate the exact injected CFU by making serial dilutions of one or more aliquots.
Inoculate appropriate dilutions on 7H10 agar plates.
Add a cohort to evaluate deposited CFU at 24 hours post-infection.
Prepare a separate syringe with needle for each animal.
Draw all 100 μL of Mtb suspension into the needle and syringe.
Vortex or pipette the Mtb suspension before drawing it into the syringe.
Warm the tail using a light source, warm water (max temperature 40°C), or heat lamp to cause vasodilation.
Hold the tail taut between the thumb and index finger.
Locate one of the two lateral tail veins in the middle third of the tail by rotating it slightly to either side.
Gently pull the tail straight toward you, holding it between your thumb and first finger approximately 2/3 of the way down the length of the tail.
Position your thumb lower than your first finger with the tail slightly bent.
With the bevel of the needle facing up and the needle parallel to the vein, steady the hub of the needle on top of your thumb.
Slide the needle forward into the tail vein until the bevel is fully inserted.
Confirm needle location by gently applying negative pressure to the plunger.
Check angle of the needle while maintaining negative pressure if no blood flash is seen.
Redirect needle until a flash of blood is observed, indicating proper placement in the vein.
Proceed with injection by smoothly depressing the plunger until solution has been fully administered.
If resistance is felt during injection or discoloration occurs around the vein, remove and reinsert new needle and syringe.
Discard used syringe/needle directly into biohazardous sharps container without recapping after injection.
Loosen restraint device and apply light pressure to puncture site with dry gauze until bleeding stops.
Place mouse back into its cage after release from restraint device.
Prepare solutions of rifampicin and SMIP-30.
Administer rifampicin through drinking water ad libitum.
Refresh antibiotic in water bottle every 2 days.
Administer SMIP-30 through intraperitoneal injection.
Inject SMIP-30 every second day.
Prepare a solution of SMIP-30.
Weigh the animals at day 0 to estimate average weight.
Calculate the required amount of SMIP-30 for each mouse based on the average weight.
Prepare aliquots of SMIP-30 in volumes sufficient for injection into individual mice.
Prepare an equal number of vehicle control aliquots as backup.
Mix rifampicin with drinking water at a concentration of 20 mg/L.
Ensure that each cage of mice has access to the rifampicin-containing drinking water.
Mix 15 mM sterile HCl to reconstitute human recombinant leptin.
Administer 200 μL of SMIP-30 or vehicle to each mouse using intraperitoneal injections.
Prepare a separate syringe with needle for each animal.
Draw the required volume of test compound or vehicle into the needle and syringe.
Restrain the mouse by its scruff tilting its head down and hold it stretched with the tail pinned by a finger.
Inject the mouse in the lower abdominal quadrant.
Identify anatomical landmarks.
Choose the lower left or right abdominal quadrant as the injection site.
Insert the needle parallel to the linea alba at a 30°–45° angle with the bevel up until the entire bevel is within the abdominal cavity.
Pull back on the plunger to ensure negative pressure before injecting.
Proceed with the injection if negative pressure is observed.
Remove the needle from the animal and discard the syringe if aspiration indicates damage to internal organs or vessels.
Administer rifampicin by placing the drinking bottle containing rifampicin solution into the cage.
Wrap the water bottles containing rifampicin in foil due to light sensitivity.
Repeat drug administrations every 2 days, with the final administration at day 13 post-infection.
Proceed to cardiac puncture and organ harvesting at day 14 post-infection.
Plate the harvested organs for colony-forming units (CFU) analysis.
Conduct body weight measurements and visual examinations during the experiment to assess health and wellbeing of the mice.
Consider any loss of body weight greater than 15% as an endpoint.
Anesthetize the mouse with isoflurane for cardiac puncture procedure.
Place the anesthetized mouse in dorsal recumbency position.
Perform cardiac puncture to collect blood from the mouse.
Confirm the mouse is deeply anesthetized by checking for the lack of pedal reflex.
Locate the xiphoid process of the sternum and insert a 25G needle with 1 cc syringe bevel up into the left ventricle of the heart.
Pull on the plunger slightly to create negative pressure inside the syringe.
If the puncture hits the heart properly, blood will automatically start filling the syringe.
Once steady blood flow into the needle has been confirmed, stabilize the needle hub and withdraw as much blood as necessary.
Observe for the absence of cardiac or respiratory cycles and perform a second physical method of euthanasia (e.g., cervical dislocation).
Incubate withdrawn blood in 1.5 mL tubes at room temperature for 30 min to allow coagulation.
Centrifuge samples at 1,000 × g for 20 min.
Transfer the serum layer to a new tube.
Immediately freeze the collected serum at -80°C.
Centrifuge the tubes at 1,000 × g for 20 minutes.
Transfer supernatant to clean tubes.
Freeze the transferred material at -80°C until cytokine analysis is performed.
Collect lungs and spleens from Mtb-infected mice immediately after cardiac puncture.
Homogenize collected organs for CFU plating.
Perform organ harvesting and CFU plating in a biological safety cabinet to maintain sterility.
Prepare GentleMacs M tubes with 2 mL of PBS-Tween for collecting lungs.
Prepare empty 1.5 mL tubes to collect spleens.
Spray scissors and forceps with 70% ethanol before use and between each mouse.
Remove skin from abdomen to chest using a sharp pair of scissors.
Cut open the peritoneum carefully and collect the spleen.
Open the diaphragm, cut the trachea carefully, and remove the lungs.
Proceed with processing and homogenization of collected organs.
Collect the spleen into a tube (Figure 6A).
Weigh each spleen using an identical empty Eppendorf tube to tare the scale.
Add 500 μL PBS-Tween to the collected spleen.
Begin homogenizing the spleen with a sterile pestle until a uniform homogenate is obtained.
Collect lungs into a GentleMacs M tube with 2 mL PBS-Tween (Figure 6D).
Homogenize the lungs using the GentleMacs dissociator to obtain a uniform homogenate.
Add 500 μL of PBS-Tween to each tube containing spleens.
Homogenize spleens using sterile pestles until a uniform homogenate is obtained.
Place each lung sample in a GentleMacs M tube with 2 mL PBS-Tween.
Run the "RNA_01" protocol twice on the GentleMacs instrument to homogenize lungs.
Prepare 1.5 mL tubes with 900 μL PBS-Tween for serial dilutions.
Transfer 100 μL of organ homogenate into the tubes containing 900 μL PBS-Tween.
Plate 100 μL of the appropriate dilution onto 7H10 agar plates.
Prepare the Mouse Inflammation Panel according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Perform serum analysis using the predefined Mouse Inflammation Panel with V-bottom plates.
Acquire data by flow cytometry on the same day as the assay protocol and preparation steps.
Analyze the cytokine and chemokine profiles from the collected data.
Set up the flow cytometer according to instructions before beginning the experiment.
Prepare the Mouse Inflammation Panel Premixed Beads as described in the manual.
Prepare the wash buffer and Matrix C as required.
Reconstitute the lyophilized Mouse Inflammation Panel Standard Cocktail according to the manual.
Thaw serum vials on ice.
Centrifuge thawed serum vials at 8,000 × g for 2 min at 4°C.
Allow all reagents to warm to 20°C–25°C before use.
Keep the plate upright during the entire assay procedure.
Wrap the plate with aluminum foil for all incubation steps.
Combine 25 μL of Matrix C and 25 μL of each standard in standard wells.
Combine 25 μL of Assay Buffer and 25 μL of mouse serum in sample wells.
Vortex mixed beads for 30 seconds.
Add 25 μL of mixed beads to each well (final volume 75 μL per well).
Mix the beads regularly during this step to avoid bead settling.
Seal the plate and cover it with aluminum foil.
Shake the plate at 800 rpm on a plate shaker for 2 hours at 20°C–25°C.
Centrifuge the plate at 1050 rpm (∼250 × g) for 5 minutes.
Remove the supernatant from each well by pipetting with a multichannel pipette.
Wash the plate once with 200 μL of wash buffer into each well.
Shake the plate at 800 rpm for 1 minute.
Repeat washing steps to remove all supernatants and excess liquid.
Add 25 μL of Detection Antibodies to each well.
Seal the plate, cover it with aluminum foil.
Shake the plate at 800 rpm on a plate shaker for 1 hour at 20°C–25°C.
At the end of incubation, add 25 μL of SA-PE to each well directly.
Seal the plate.
Cover it with aluminum foil.
Shake at 800 rpm on a plate shaker for 30 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Add 150 μL of 1× Wash Buffer to each well.
Resuspend the beads by pipetting.
Read the samples on a flow cytometer.
Resuspend the beads by pipetting often during reading.
Add a wash step with water every 16 samples.
Set the flow rate to low and set the number of beads to be acquired to about 300 per analyte (4000 beads for a 13-plex assay).
Create a large gate to include both Beads A and Beads B (gate A+B).
Proceed with data analysis using BioLegend’s LEGENDplex™ data analysis software.
